article_title: «Путін грає в матрьошку»: як Росія намагається прив’язати Україну до глобальних торгів
article_content:
«Путін грає в матрьошку»: як Росія намагається прив’язати Україну до глобальних торгів
Перспективи переговорів між Володимиром Зеленським і Путіним залишаються сумнівними.
Російський диктатор Путін не демонструє готовності припиняти агресію проти України. Натомість Кремль намагається використати переговорний процес для досягнення ширших геополітичних цілей.
Таку оцінку в етері Еспресо озвучив голова правління Інституту світової політики Віктор Шлінчак.
Експерт скептично ставиться до можливості проведення результативних переговорів між президентом України Володимиром Зеленським і російським диктатором. На його думку, передумов для припинення війни з боку Москви наразі немає.
«Я скептично ставлюся до того, що Путін коли-небудь, в принципі, сяде за стіл переговорів із Зеленським і буде щось підписувати. Ви розумієте, що для того, щоб навіть щось підписати, ці документи мають бути погоджені. Я не бачу поки що намірів Росії зупиняти агресію. Тому що через агресію в Україні вони намагаються зіграти в більш глобальні процеси», — зазначив Шлінчак.
За словами аналітика, Росія прагне поєднати питання Донбасу з іншими претензіями до західних держав, зокрема щодо системи безпеки в Європі. Москва знову порушує тему виведення іноземних військових контингентів із держав НАТО, які приєдналися до Альянсу після 1999 року.
«Вже ж з’явилося в порядку денному, що давайте будемо обговорювати паралельно історію Донбасу, прив’яжемо її до того, щоб повернемось до Варшавського договору і, власне, країни НАТО, які з 1999 року стали членами Альянсу, повинні вивести іноземні контингенти. Маються на увазі американські, німецькі, французькі. Тобто, починаються, взагалі, торги про інше», — пояснив експерт.
Шлінчак вважає, що Кремль розглядає українське питання не ізольовано, а як засіб впливу на інші міжнародні домовленості. За його словами, Путін послідовно намагається пов’язувати різні конфлікти та переговорні процеси між собою.
«У мене завжди є відчуття, що Путін грає в „матрьошку“. Тобто, спочатку був Крим, який був прив’язаний до політичної позиції в Києві. Потім сталася повномасштабна війна, яку він зараз прив’язує куди завгодно. Він Трампа починає ув’язувати з переговорами по Ірану, починає обіцяти йому, що він закриє йому ту війну, відповідно, давайте будемо мінятися», — сказав він.
Окремо експерт застеріг від спроб сприймати російську агресію як локальний конфлікт, після завершення якого відносини з Москвою нібито можна буде відновити у звичному форматі.
На його переконання, якщо Росію не зупинити в Україні, загроза поширення агресії залишатиметься актуальною і для інших європейських держав. Шлінчак також звернув увагу на те, що частина європейських політиків досі розраховує на повернення до нормальних відносин із Москвою та відновлення доступу до дешевого російського газу.
«Якщо в Україні Путіна не зупинити, Росії не зупинити, то вся ця агресія піде далі. Мені просто дуже дивно, що в Європі до цього часу думають, що вони якось переживуть цю війну і потім повернуться до нормалізації стосунків і до дешевого російського газу», — наголосив експерт.
Раніше повідомлялося, що президент України Володимир Зеленський заявив, що питання вимог Москви можна порушувати лише після завершення війни та забезпечення надійних гарантій безпеки для України.
Ми раніше інформували, що у Кремлі поставили під сумнів швидке проведення тристороннього саміту Путіна, Трампа і Зеленського.
description: Перспективи переговорів між Володимиром Зеленським і Путіним залишаються сумнівними.

article_title: «Часы тикают»: США и Китай призвали не откладывать меры по контролю над ИИ
article_content:
США отстают от Китая в сфере государственного регулирования искусственного интеллекта и подходят к саммиту Трампа и Си Цзиньпина в Шэньчжэне без четкой стратегии. В то же время в самих разработках Америка лидирует благодаря Anthropic и OpenAI. Стоит договориться хотя бы об узких правилах и экспертном канале для обсуждения опасных инцидентов, написал обозреватель The Washington Post Дэвид Игнатиус.
Безопасность искусственного интеллекта следует воспринимать как гонку со временем. Никто не знает, каких опасностей следует ожидать. Когда две сверхдержавы наконец-то всерьёз сядут за стол переговоров, может быть уже слишком поздно, чтобы предотвратить катастрофу. Шанс предоставит встреча Трампа и Си Цзиньпина в Шэньчжэне в следующем месяце. Это будет их третий саммит в этом году. Приедет и президент России Владимир Путин, но, по мнению автора, «его единственной задачей должно быть предотвращение катастрофы, которую он уже устроил в Украине».
США лидируют в технологической гонке, однако согласованного плана безопасности у них нет. Президент говорит об ИИ как о глобальном бою UFC: «Кто победит в ИИ, тот и выиграет». Министр финансов Скотт Бессент вторит ему: «Если [Китай] оторвется от нас в сфере ИИ, то больше ничего не будет иметь значения».
На более низких уровнях власти политика в сфере ИИ разрознена и непоследовательна. Судя по всему, механизм принятия решений через Совет национальной безопасности не работает. Поэтому технология, которая может иметь такие же глобальные последствия, как ядерное оружие, развивается сама по себе. Бессент возглавляет американскую сторону переговоров с Пекином по ИИ, но как их организовать, пока неясно.
В Китае единую национальную стратегию формулирует Си Цзиньпин. Такой подход, вероятно, возможен лишь в однопартийной командной экономике. Пекин не противопоставляет безопасность развитию технологии. «Новый китайский подход — это не “безопасность ИИ против развития ИИ”. Это попытка сделать безопасность совместимой с быстрым развитием всё более мощных систем, а зачастую и способствующей ему, сохраняя широкие полномочия вмешиваться всякий раз, когда речь идет о политических интересах или национальной безопасности», — написал бывший аналитик правительства США по вопросам Китая Пол Триоло.
Пекин также понимает, что в этой гонке может проиграть. Бывший эксперт Совета национальной безопасности США по Китаю Джулиан Гевирц объяснил в недавней статье: китайцы видят в ИИ «технологию, где победитель получает все и которая может позволить американской мощи расти быстрее, чем соперники успеют догнать, сделав ее лидерство постоянным». Он назвал это «рекурсивным преимуществом».
Большую сделку с Китаем вряд ли удастся заключить, рассказала автору бывшая высокопоставленная сотрудница Агентства национальной безопасности США Энн Нойбергер, которая при администрации Джо Байдена отвечала за ИИ. Однако «мы, вероятно, могли бы договориться об узких правилах безопасности, чтобы избежать катастрофы, и создать экспертный канал для обсуждения опасных инцидентов», — сказала она.
Контроль над ядерным оружием в 1960-х и 1970-х годах начинался с небольших шагов. Подобный подход может сработать и в сфере ИИ. Впрочем, ядерное оружие не умело писать собственные инструкции, а ИИ, вероятно, скоро сможет. Колонку автор завершает словами: «Часы тикают, и никто не знает, когда пробьет полночь».
В октябре Белый дом обязал разработчиков суперинтеллекта немедленно сообщать о сбоях в работе их моделей. Какие санкции ждут нарушителей, не уточнили. До этого США полагались преимущественно на добровольные обязательства.
В конце сентября президент и руководители Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, X и NVIDIA подписали одностраничное соглашение о безопасности с четырьмя уровнями надзора, в том числе внешним аудитом.
О том, почему каждое обновление ИИ становится риском для цивилизации и помогут ли законы, в статье ZN.UA «Игра в рулетку с суперинтеллектом. Почему каждое обновление ИИ становится риском для цивилизации» пишет заведующий Научной лабораторией иммерсивных технологий и права Института информации, безопасности и права Национальной академии правовых наук Украины, доктор наук в области права Алексей Костенко.
description: В Шэньчжэне Трамп и Си могут согласовать минимальные правила в отношении искусственного интеллекта и обмен данными об опасных сбоях.

article_title: How will John Healey’s energy support package affect you?
article_content:
How will John Healey’s energy support package affect you?
Chancellor’s ‘new course’ includes a £100 one-off payment, low-carbon upgrade loans and an end to standing charges
John Healey has unveiled a package of support for households being buffeted by “global economic storms”.
“I’m setting a new course to get energy costs down in line with Europe,” the chancellor said in his maiden budget. In the long term, he hopes that changes in how Britain covers the cost of renewables and grid upgrades will “drive down all aspects of energy bills”.
British households face some of the highest energy charges for three years, with the war in the Middle East driving up oil and gas prices.
Under the government’s price cap, average dual-fuel bills are £1,700 a year and could rise to more than £2,100 a year from January, according to industry forecasts.
So what has the chancellor offered hard-pressed households to help them through the coldest months of the year? And will it be enough to lower gas and electricity bills?
The £100 ‘household energy payment’
The government’s biggest bet on offering “breathing space” to struggling households this winter is a one-off payment of £100 in January for 20m households in council tax bands A to D. It is also the measure most likely to deliver real benefit for those in need.
The £2.6bn “household energy payment” will go directly into bank accounts to “take the pressure off in the coldest months and see people through to the spring”, according to Healey.
Martin Lewis, the founder of MoneySavingExpert.com, said households could face a 25% cost increase from January and shouldn’t expect to feel better off than they do today.
Officials are anxious to avoid handing public money to those who can get by without it but they lack household income data to target proposed support. Using council tax bands is “the least worst proxy”, Lewis said.
The payment will be in addition to the Warm Home Discount, which offers about 6m means-tested households in England, Wales and Scotland £150 off winter fuel bills.
This measure will offer a modest saving for most British households – but not all, and perhaps not until next winter.
Healey promised to end “unfair and outdated” standing charges on gas bills for 23m homes “in 2027 or as soon as possible after”. This could help almost two-thirds of households to save an average of £45 a year.
A standing charge is a fixed daily fee paid through all household gas bills, regardless of how much is used. It means homes that severely ration their gas use – or use none at all – still shoulder the same cost as a high-income household.
The charge typically adds about £100 a year to bills and the change means these costs will soon be recovered through a higher unit price for gas. For those with below-average gas use, bills should fall. But there won’t be savings for everyone.
Jonny Marshall, an economist at the Resolution Foundation, said households with high gas use might have higher bills when the unit rate increases. These could include low-income households who have bigger families or poorly insulated homes.
A home using 7,000 kilowatt hours of gas a year would save about £40 under the change, but a household using 14,000 kWh of gas a year could be £25 worse off, according to Richard Neudegg, a director at Uswitch.com. A household using the typical 11,500 kWh shouldn’t see any change, he added.
Removing standing charges from gas bills will help two-thirds of households save an average of £45 a year. Photograph: Paul Melling/Alamy
Lower electricity levies
The government has already begun taking aim at taxes and policy costs loaded on to electricity bills that could over time mean removing hundreds of pounds from bills.
This month, it removed the 5% VAT levy on electricity bills for 29m households, effectively saving them about £45 a year.
This was supposed to help households through the coldest months of the year, until March. But Healey has promised to keep VAT off bills until July, extending the annual savings to £50 a year, according to the Treasury.
The move follows a string of cuts to electricity levies over the past year which have shaved about £150 a year off costs.
“For many years, under Conservative governments, policy costs were simply loaded on to household bills through levies,” Healey said. “Today, I am putting an end to that. We’ll introduce a new cost control framework to drive down all aspects of energy bills.”
Healey confirmed he would consider steps to remove standing charges on electricity too, which add about £200 a year to the average bill. The savings from this measure remain unclear, depending on which costs would move into general taxation and which would be covered through the unit price for electricity.
Healey will continue to alter a subsidy scheme for the UK’s oldest renewable energy projects, around three-quarters of which has been removed from bills and covered by general taxation. The research charity Nesta said this would lower electricity costs by £42 a year.
Healey has scrapped plans for a levy to support hydrogen projects that would otherwise have added £2.60 to £4.50 a year to the average dual-fuel bill.
Low-carbon home upgrades
The government believes that households could save up to £550 a year on energy bills if they invest in solar panels, home batteries and a heat pump. These savings could rise by a further £300 a year with a time-of-use tariff, according to the government.
To help households access these savings, a Warm Home Loans scheme, which launched on Tuesday, will offer government-backed loans of up to £35,000 for low-carbon energy alternatives.
The government said it was committed to rolling out heat pumps through its boiler upgrade scheme, which provides grants of up to £7,500 to help meet the £13,600 cost of installing one.
Grants of up to £9,000 a year are available to households that are not connected to the gas grid and rely on high-cost heating oil.
Energy debt relief
For many, the government’s new measures will come too late to help this winter. But there could be support in the spring from a debt relief scheme.
The government said the delayed scheme will “provide targeted support to customers in genuine financial need”. Total household energy debt has tripled from 2021 to a record £5bn and could reach £7bn by the end of the year.
The one-off, targeted intervention has been designed to help those with debts from the 2022-24 energy crisis and little prospect of repaying them.
Nesta has suggested debt relief could be given to about 2m households for a one-off cost of £2.7bn. This would also cut the £29 a year paid by all households to cover the cost of unpaid bills.
More details on the scheme will follow in early 2027, the government said.

article_title: Budget 2026: Healey hikes taxes on banks and landlords to fund £100 handouts to 20m households
article_content:
John Healey raised taxes on banks and landlords to fund a £100 winter handout for 20 million families as official forecasts made clear there is no end in sight for the cost of living crisis.
In his first budget, the chancellor blamed “global economic storms” for the grim outlook, as the war in Iran drives up oil and gas prices.
But he also faced criticism for failing to squeeze more money from profitable banks, punishing savers and not giving enough help to the poorest.
In a low-key speech designed with febrile bond markets in mind, Healey was at pains to stress he was sticking to Labour’s self-imposed fiscal rules, and there were few surprises in his hour-long address to MPs.
But with households facing soaring energy prices, and mortgage bills rising amid higher interest rates, Healey offered a £100 cost-of-living payout, which will be sent to all English households in council tax bands A-D.
It formed the centrepiece of a cost of living package, which he said would “take the pressure off in the coldest months, and see people through to the spring”.
The £2.6bn cost of the £100 giveaway includes funding for the Scottish and Welsh governments, which Healey said he hoped they would use to implement a similar scheme.
“I know that with the conflict in the Middle East, rising energy bills are a real worry. I know that people look to government at times like this, not to solve all their problems, but to give them a bit of breathing space,” he said.
But the government’s independent forecaster warned households face a “grim picture” on living standards, as it slashed the outlook for the economy in 2027 and said there was “virtually no growth” in disposable income for households.
Healey also came under fire for an unexpected 2p increase in tax rates for income earned on property or savings. As well as hitting savers and landlords, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said it risks “leading to a steady rise in rents”, by deterring landlords from the market and cutting supply, as well as passing on costs to tenants.
Ruth Curtice, the chief executive of the Resolution Foundation thinktank, criticised the £100 handout, arguing it would have been better to give more generous support to the poorest consumers.
“The chancellor has missed the mark with badly targeted support that has left families facing a tough winter as energy bills rise,” she said.
As expected, the chancellor also cancelled fuel tax rises planned by Rachel Reeves, and extended the VAT cut on electricity prices previously announced to next summer.
Healey announced several measures intended to cut businesses’ costs – including raising the rates relief threshold from £12,000 to £18,000 for companies in the retail, hospitality and leisure sectors. The change would be funded by higher taxes on gambling and vape shops, he said.
The cost of the household support measures will be met by a doubling of the additional levy banks pay on their profits, to 6%; as well as the higher taxes on income from property and savings.
The additional bank tax will only last for 15 months and marked a less significant rise than some in the industry had feared. Banks’ share prices were among the highest risers in the blue chip FTSE 100 index on Wednesday.
Laura Suter, director of personal finance at AJ Bell, said: “Savers will be hit with another hefty tax rise on their savings interest, adding to the squeeze on their savings over the past few years.”
She added that the higher tax on rental income “could be passed on to tenants, with rent hikes a potential lever for landlords to mitigate any increase in tax”.
“Equally, we could see yet more landlords selling up, in favour of investing their money in other assets that have lower taxes and less government tinkering,” she said.
The New Economics Foundation thinktank accused Healey of failing to be bold enough. Hannah Peaker, its deputy chief executive, said: “As households prepare to be hit by a wave of price rises this winter, the chancellor has shown the right instincts but not yet the right scale.
“The £100 support with energy bills will provide some welcome relief, but the chancellor could have been braver in the face of what we are up against.”
Energy provider EDF predicts that the Ofgem price cap – which determines consumer bills – is set to go up by £466 in January. And despite Healey’s promise of a “breathing space,” in the teeth of the crisis, official forecasts published by the OBR alongside the budget pointed to a challenging winter.
Presenting the forecasts, the OBR’s David Miles highlighted a “pretty grim picture” for household finances, as inflation rises to almost 4%.
Even by 2030-31, it only expects real disposable household incomes – its favoured measure of living standards – to be 2% higher than before the Covid pandemic. It now expects anaemic economic growth of 1% next year, about half a percentage point lower than expected in March.
Healey said higher inflation and interest rates had hit the government’s finances too, ratcheting up the government’s interest bill by £14bn this year alone, but promised to stick to Labour’s fiscal rules.
The OBR said Healey would meet the most important rule – to balance day-to-day spending with tax revenues – with a diminished headroom of £15bn by the target date of 2029-30, against the £24bn Rachel Reeves had built up in the spring.
Borrowing is scheduled to be higher than expected in the short term, but the chancellor promised to rebuild the buffer against the rules to £22bn by the end of the five-year forecast period.
“That is what a buffer is for. Use it when you need it, rebuild it when you can,” he said. Bond markets appeared unruffled by the higher-than-expected borrowing.
The deferral of some important decisions to next year’s spending review prompted the Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, to argue Burnham was keeping his options open on an early general election.
Burnham doubled down on his promise not to call one, however, telling reporters on Wednesday that he could rule one out for at least 12 months. “I’m not thinking about my own party and its prospects. I am thinking about people, and I’m thinking about what I can do to help them.”
Badenoch said Britain had “overspent, overborrowed and overtaxed”, and criticised Healey for delayed decisions on defence spending and welfare cuts. Healey has said he will tackle welfare after reports from Alan Milburn on youth unemployment and Sir Stephen Timms on disability benefits, expected next month.
Helen Miller, the director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that by sticking to the tight spending plans bequeathed by Reeves, Healey could be storing up trouble for the spending review due next year.
“History warns us to be sceptical of tight spending plans in later years of the forecast. Next year’s spending review will be a crunch point, and looks very tough for many departments, whose budgets will be squeezed by higher inflation forecasts,” she said.
“The plans for overall spending set out in the budget mean that spending choices at next year’s spending review will be much harder than those made so far this parliament.”
Buried in the budget was a hint at an easing of some migration restrictions, including some industries that will be allowed to lower the salary thresholds for visas to allow companies across the country to hire international talent.
Among the winners was London mayor Lord Sadiq Khan, who received new powers to extend the Bakerloo line in London and a pledge that cross-Channel trains will now also stop at Stratford International in east London. There was also cash to explore hosting the Olympics in “a northern city” – and former Greater Manchester mayor Burnham may have a candidate city in mind.
author: Heather Stewart, Jessica Elgot and Richard Partington

article_title: ‘They mobilized a whole government response to that joke’: Obama laughs off Trump attacks in rally for Ossoff
article_content:
Barack Obama, speaking at a Wednesday campaign rally in suburban Atlanta, offered a closing argument for Democrats in the final week of the midterm election campaign.
“These are not serious people,” he said of Donald Trump and the Republican party. “And we’re all paying the price for their lack of seriousness.”
Obama came to Georgia to support the campaigns of US senator Jon Ossoff, former Atlanta mayor and gubernatorial hopeful Keisha Lance Bottoms, and an array of down-ballot Democrats as part of his cross-country campaign tour before next week’s election. From 3,500 to 4,000 people filled the Discovery Center of Clayton county for the late election season stop, just south of Atlanta.
Obama has been casting caltrops behind him with each campaign stop, offering pointed criticism of Republican candidates and Donald Trump that has been unusual for the former president. He continued to do so on Wednesday, again invoking the image of Trump’s gilded renovations of the White House and noting Trump’s strident reaction to his crack last week likening it to Saddam Hussein decorating a Cheesecake Factory.
“The Saddam Hussein thing didn’t bother him. But he was very upset about the Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said. “I mean, it’s all crazy, but this is the crazy part: they mobilized a whole government response to that joke.
“The White House even called the secretary of the treasury,” the former president continued. “The guy who is trying to figure out how to lower inflation … they told him he should hold a press conference in front of the Cheesecake Factory.”
He also rebuffed Republicans’ accusations of snobbery for referencing the popular chain restaurant.
“I am the father of two daughters,” Obama said. “Do you think I could have survived their childhood without going to the Cheesecake Factory?”
But he turned that discussion to the problems of affordability for American voters, in contrast with the corruption of the presidency.
“We have never seen a president so intent on selling favors,” Obama said. “The guy has made billions of dollars while in office. Understand that this has not been done in modern times.”
The construction of a new ballroom on the site of the former East Wing of the White House featured in the comments of many speakers at Wednesday’s rally, including Ossoff.
“Each day, Donald Trump digs the moral pit deeper,” Ossoff said, accusing the president of leading “the most corrupt administration of all time, and everybody knows it”.
“If you’re involved in any of this, next year you’ll be raising your hand to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth,” Ossoff said, in reference to Democrats pledging to impeach Trump if they take control of Congress next year.
The crowd chanted: “Lock him up!” in response.
Bottoms, meanwhile, contrasted her candidacy with that of her Republican opponent Rick Jackson, tying the billionaire healthcare executive to Trump and describing them as “two out-of-touch billionaires who want to keep getting rich on the backs of taxpayers”.
Invoking the legacies of US Representative John Lewis and Coretta Scott King, Bottoms characterized her candidacy as transcending politics. “They may have the money, but they will never overtake our movement,” she said.
Despite a broad wave of Democratic support buoying candidates across the country – and the eight- to 10-point polling lead Ossoff has on his Republican opponent, US Representative Mike Collins – Bottoms is statistically tied in polls with Jackson. If elected, Bottoms would break the state’s Republican trifecta – where the GOP has controlled both chambers of the legislature and the governor’s office – which began in 2004.
Rev Raphael Warnock, Georgia’s other senator, warned of “spiritual wickedness in high places” while describing the effects of deep cuts to Medicaid and Snap nutrition support for children.
“This is about the character of the country,” Warnock said. “This is about who we are and whether we are here for one another … I am concerned about the spiritual health of our country. There is brokenness, because only a broken nation could manage to elect Donald Trump twice.”
Trump, who was campaigning in Ohio at the same time as the Georgia rally, has also been on a national rally blitz, holding near-daily events in the final days of the midterm campaign. Trump has made two appearances in as many weeks in Georgia, both in what would otherwise seem to be congressional districts that are safe territory for Republicans.
author: George Chidi in Atlanta

article_title: Judge rebuffs Trump DoJ’s bid to force California to set aside 20,000 ballots
article_content:
A federal judge declined to order California election officials to segregate and not count ballots from people the Trump administration claimed were non-citizens, rebuffing a legally thin request from the justice department that appeared designed to cast doubt over the results of the midterms.
The ruling from US district judge David Carter, nominated to the federal bench by Bill Clinton, comes about two weeks after the justice department delivered a USB drive to election officials in Los Angeles and Sacramento that it said contained the names of 20,000 non-citizens on the state’s voter rolls. There are more than 23 million registered voters in California and non-citizen voting is extremely rare.
“This case is about the right of every American citizen to vote in a free and fair election,” Carter wrote in his Wednesday evening ruling. “Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch.”
“In bringing this lawsuit, the Executive would have this Court believe that it reigns as a sole sovereign,” Carter continued. “But California and its people are sovereign, too.”
The justice department gave officials just 48 hours to review the list and said it would sue the state if officials did not sequester ballots from those whose citizenship it could not confirm. The department refused to provide more details about its methodology and Los Angeles officials found preliminary indicators the list was inaccurate. The justice department then sued California on 15 October to try and force the state to sequester the ballots and verify citizenship.
If the justice department’s request were granted, Carter wrote, it would likely violate a 1993 law that requires states to strike ineligible voters from its official lists no later than 90 days before an election.
California election officials have said they cannot verify the citizenship of those on the agency’s list before election day. Carter chastised the justice department’s directive as risking the disenfranchisement of thousands of voters. “A ballot segregated, in effect, would be a ballot removed,” Carter wrote.
The justice department separately has threatened to prosecute election officials in the state if they tabulate ballots from non-citizens. Such a move would be without a legal basis, Sam Trepel, a former prosecutor at the justice department, wrote in a blogpost this month. After filing the lawsuit, the Trump administration began providing lists to other counties of suspected non-citizen voters. When election officials began reviewing them, they found the department had flagged voters who were not on the rolls and had provided insufficient information to verify their citizenship status, according to CalMatters.
Carter’s ruling came after the justice department tried to bypass him entirely. After Carter set a 27 October hearing on the justice department’s emergency motion, the department took the unusual step of appealing to the US court of appeals for the ninth circuit, saying Carter was not considering the case fast enough. A panel of ninth circuit judges ruled 2-1 against the justice department earlier this week.
Legal experts have been skeptical about the justice department’s efforts in California since the outset. In July, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced it had identified up to 190,000 non-citizens on California voter rolls. The DHS did not provide more details to the state until after ballots had already gone out in the state.
“Eroded trust in our democracy is irreparable. Once a vote is segregated, lasting harm has occurred. If the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger,” Carter wrote in his Wednesday opinion. “This Court declines to be a party to such process.”

article_title: Туреччина готова відновити переговори між Україною та Росією: Ердоган звернувся до Трампа
article_content:
Туреччина готова відновити переговори між Україною та Росією: Ердоган звернувся до Трампа
Туреччина готова долучитися до зусиль із відновлення переговорного процесу між Україною та Росією задля припинення війни.
Президент Туреччини Реджеп Таїп Ердоган висловив готовність Анкари допомогти відновити дипломатичні контакти між Україною та Росією, щоб сприяти завершенню війни.
Про це повідомила канцелярія турецького лідера в соціальній мережі X.
З відповідною заявою Ердоган виступив під час телефонної розмови з президентом США Дональдом Трампом.
«Президент Ердоган підкреслив, що Туреччина готова зробити свій внесок у зусилля, спрямовані на відновлення дипломатичного процесу між Україною та Росією задля припинення війни», — йдеться в повідомленні канцелярії.
Окрім перспектив відновлення переговорів, лідери обговорили двосторонні відносини між Туреччиною та Сполученими Штатами, а також актуальні регіональні й міжнародні питання.
Раніше повідомлялося, що президент Туреччини Реджеп Таїп Ердоган заявив, що війна між Росією та Україною має закінчитися за умови повного збереження українського суверенітету та кордонів.
Ми раніше інформували, що у Кремлі поставили під сумнів швидке проведення тристороннього саміту Путіна, Трампа і Зеленського.

article_title: Obama mocks Trump’s response to Cheesecake Factory jibe. ‘They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke!’ – as it happened
article_content:
Obama mocks Trump's response to Cheesecake Factory jibe. 'They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke, not to inflation, but to that joke!'
We are still watching simultaneous rallies, for Republicans in Ohio, and for Democrats in Georgia, that have overlapped in interesting ways at times.
Minutes ago in Ohio, Donald Trump responded his indignation to his predecessor Barack Obama’s joke that “he’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.”
“I paid for it myself. I fixed it, and now it’s more beautiful and in better shape,” Trump said, defending the quality of his renovations to the White House. “President Obama,” he added, was miffed because he is someone “who doesn’t understand cleanliness, who doesn’t understand broken, cracked stone and sidewalk, who doesn’t understand that having asphalt going to your main entrance is not the right thing”.
A short time later in Georgia, Obama repeated his jibe and then reflected on the outraged response to his joke.
“The guy is building a ballroom that is bigger than the White House. He’s paved over the Rose Garden, put a helicopter pad on the South Lawn, and there is gold everywhere. So much gold,” Obama said. “This is a fact, I’m not making this up. He, the president of the United States, is spending time super-gluing gold medallions to the mantel in the Oval Office. I am not making this up. He is literally doing arts and crafts while we are fighting a war and trying to deal with out-of-control prices.”
“I heard the president was not happy when I joked over the weekend that he’s got the white House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” the former president said. “First of all, let me get this on the record: I am the father of two daughters. Do you think, could have survived their childhood without going to the Cheesecake Factory?”
“Chucky Cheese and California Pizza Kitchen and the Cheesecake Factory – that was my jam for about a decade,” Obama said.
“The interesting thing about how the administration responded to the speech I gave the other day. They did not dispute what I said about them being directly responsible for rising prices. They did not argue with that,” Obama continued. “They did not deny tariffs were contributing to higher costs for families. They didn’t say anything about that. I accused this administration, based on the facts, that they were engaging in unprecedented levels of corruption. They didn’t say anything about that. The president wasn’t even mad about the Saddam Hussein comparison. That part didn’t bother him, but he was very upset about the Cheesecake Factory comments. He took great umbrage. He said, I didn’t understand the work of the artisans in the White House.”
“It’s all crazy, but this was the really crazy part,” Obama added. “They mobilized a whole of government response to that joke - not to inflation, but to that joke.”
“The White House even called the secretary of the treasury – this is the man who is in charge of the economy, the person who’s supposed to be figuring out how to make your life more affordable, the guy who’s supposed to be figuring out how to lower inflation and reduce interest rates. They told him he should hold a press conference in front of the Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said, to laughter from the crowd.

Trump again defends Ramaswamy ad featuring Amy Acton's mother, who sided with husband accused of raping her pre-teen daughter
Speaking in Ohio on Wednesday, Donald Trump doubled down on his support of an attack ad released by the Republican candidate for governor, Vivek Ramaswamy, which features criticism of his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton, from her estranged mother, who lost custody of her daughter at age 12, when her second husband was accused of raping her daughter.
Trump, who was asked last Friday by Monica Alba of NBC News, “do the sexual abuse allegations mean nothing to you?” again ignored that aspect of the story and complained that Ramaswamy was being treated “unfairly” by the media.
“The mother said that Amy Acton, the daughter, is a liar, that she’s no good, that she lied about the opponent, how the hell is that his problem?” Trump asked, referrign to Ramaswamy, who was widely criticized by both Republican and Democratic officials for releasing the ad.
“He had the mother of his opponent say that her daughter was a liar,” Trump said. “The fake news criticized him.”
The president then argued, as he has before, that if is mother had said something like that about him, and it was used in an ad, no one in the media would have objected and “the press would be getting Pulitzer prizes.” He again refused to acknowledge that his hypothetical excluded the serious sexual abuse allegations Acton’s mother is accused of ignoring.
Trump also accused Alaska Democrats of “cheating” for reportedly working to recruit a candidate named Dan Sullivan to be on the ballot in a US Senate race there against the Republican incumbent, Dan Sullivan. The president called for the Democratic candidate Mary Peltola to be prosecuted, but made no mention of what law he thinks she violated.
“Nobody can tell the difference. This is voter fraud at the highest level and the Democrat candidate who is involved in the scheme, Mary Peltola, who said she didn’t know anything about it” Trump said, “she should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted, and so should the fake Dan Sullivan.”
'We got to keep reality TV on Bravo," Obama says, 'We don’t need it in the White House'
Both Donald Trump and Barack Obama have now finished speaking at dueling rallies in Ohio and Georgia.
“We need serious people in Washington and state capitals, these are serious times, Obama said near the end of his remarks in Atlanta, in support of the Democratic nominee for governor, Keisha Lance Bottoms and senator Jon Ossoff.
“We seem to constantly just tolerate unseriousness. The people who are currently in charge, they’re not doing their homework. They’re not they’re not doing their work. They’re not presenting realistic plans,” Obama said. “These are people who are more interested in performance and flexing and texting and putting people down rather than lifting them up.”
“They enjoy insulting and dividing instead of bringing people together to solve problems,” he added. “I know we’re in Atlanta and I want y’all to know Michelle has love for the Real Housewives. But we got to keep reality TV on Bravo. Leave it to the professionals. We don’t need it in the White House. We don’t need it in the governor’s mansion. We need people like John and Keisha in there.”
In contrast, Trump wound up his remarks by having his supporters watch television – specifically a CNN clip from a month ago that showed he remains very popular with people who describe themselves as “Maga Republicans”. The president did not mention that this clip was taken from a much longer segment that detailed just how unpopular he is with everyone else, including non-Maga Republicans.

'Trump went on the Jeffrey Epstein plane!' heckler shouts at Trump rally in Ohio
Donald Trump is 40 minutes into his remarks in Ohio, where he was heckled over his ties to Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted child sex offender he socialized with for at least 17 years.
During a pause in the president’s remarks, a man shouted: “Trump went on the Jeffrey Epstein plane!” before being removed from the crowd.
“He mentioned Epstein. So I threw Jeffrey Epstein out of a club like 20 years ago, because I thought he was a whack job. That was a great thing I did, I must say,” Trump said. “I threw Jeffrey Epstein the hell out of Mar-a-Lago. And I was the one that was totally exonerated from him.”
While Trump’s aides have repeatedly claimed that Trump banned Epstein from Mar-a-Lago “because he was a creep”, the president has explained the falling out with his old friend differently, saying that the reason was that Epstein “stole people that worked for me”.
Last year, when a reporter asked Trump if one of the people he was referring to was the late Virginia Giuffre, one of Epstein’s most prominent accusers who said in a lawsuit that she was hired away from the Mar-a-Lago spa by Epstein’s accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell in 2000, when she was 16.
Giuffre, who died last year, alleged in her complaint that she was first abused by Epstein and Maxwell together, and then “lent out to other powerful men”, including then Prince Andrew.
“I think she worked at the spa,” Trump replied then. “I think so. I think that was one of the people, yeah. He stole her. And by the way, she had no complaints about us, as you know. None whatsoever.”
The president’s claim that one of the employees Epstein “stole” from him, leading to their break, was the 16-year-old Giuffre complicated the timeline. Giuffre was hired away from Mar-a-Lago in 2000, but two years later, Trump spoke highly of Epstein to a reporter.
“I’ve known Jeff for 15 years. Terrific guy,” Trump told New York magazine in late 2002. “He’s a lot of fun to be with. It is even said that he likes beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side.”
Sarah Blaskey, a Miami Herald investigative reporter, also pointed out in her 2020 book on Mar-a-Lago that Epstein remained on the membership rolls of Mar-a-Lago until October 2007, more than a year after he was first arrested and charged with soliciting prostitution from a minor.
As Trump boasts about Iran war in Ohio, Ossoff mocks his claims in Georgia
At rallies occurring at the same time, Donald Trump just boasted in Ohio about what he calls the great success of his war in Iran, while Jon Ossoff, in Georgia, mocked Trump for that war and other failures.
Trump made no mention of the fact that the war with Iran he started in February is still not over, and repeated his lie that the war was necessary to prevent Iran from making a nuclear weapon.
“While the crook president and his crook family rake in billions from all over the world, you pay more for everything,” Ossoff told Georgians. “They lied us into war and spent most of the last year covering up for the world’s most famous pedophile.”
“Now remember, they also promised peace. They promised peace. Instead, today marks eight months of a needless war that the useless, draft-dodging commander-in-chief can’t figure out how to end or how to win,” Ossoff continued.
“Remember last year, last year they claimed Iran’s nuclear program had been obliterated? Do you remember that? And then this year, they told us it posed an imminent threat. Both times lies,” he added.
“On day four of the war, day four, the president declared victory,” he continued. “On day 11, Trump said, quote, ‘the war is very complete’. Day 13, quote, ‘we won’. Day 21, ‘getting very close’. Day 32, quote ‘leaving very soon’. On day 40, the president declared, quote, ‘total and complete victory’. Today is day 243. Twenty one Americans are dead and hundreds wounded. Iran still has its uranium and drones and missiles while diesel hits its all time high. They’ve drained our stockpiles to achieve nothing while the president builds himself a victory arch.”
Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens' fiancé says he is voting for Republican Mike Rogers, not Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
Jason Turkish, who is engaged to be married to Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens, appeared at a campaign event for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan on Wednesday and told reporters that he was voting for the Republican, not Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who narrowly defeated Stevens in the Democratic primary in August.
Turkish, a disabilities and civil rights lawyer, said at a Republican Jewish Coalition event for Rogers that El-Sayed’s refusal to say that Iran was a greater threat to the United States than Israel in the first general election debate was “100% disqualifying to be a United States senator”.
Turkish, described by Jewish Insider as “a prominent Jewish Democrat in Michigan”, said that El-Sayed’s rhetoric “makes folks unsafe”.
“When he says genocide over and over,” Turkish said of El-Sayed’s criticism of Israel’s destruction of Gaza, “he makes my community less safe.”
“We’ve never seen a candidate for US Senate act so recklessly toward the safety of Jews in the community as we have from Abdul,” Turkish told the Detroit News.
According to the Detroit News, Turkish has donated Democrats and Republicans, including $200,000 to Democratic candidates in the midterm elections and over $24,000 to support Maine Republican Susan Collins.
Donald Trump is scheduled to speak soon at a rally for Republican candidates in Chillicothe, Ohio, where the party’s nominee for governor, Vivek Ramaswamy, and the sitting senator Jon Husted, have already spoken.
Meanwhile in Georgia, Barack Obama is waiting to address a Democratic rally in Atlanta, in support of the party’s nominee for governor, Keisha Lance Bottoms and sitting senator Jon Ossoff.
Bottoms and Ossoff are scheduled to speak immediately before Obama. The Georgia rally is running about 30 minutes behind schedule, meaning that it is likely that Trump and Obama will be speaking at the same time.
As we watch the simultaneous rallies for in Ohio and Georgia, we are currently being treated to a musical split-screen.
Janelle Monáe is currently performing live in Atlanta, following a performance by the HBCU Clark Atlanta University marching band, while Trump supporters in Ohio are being treated to his rally playlist, which includes songs from a number of artists who sued to have him stop using their music. The crowd is currently listening to Sinéad O’Connor’s version of Nothing Compares 2 U, which her estate said in 2024 she would have been “disgusted, hurt, and insulted” to have used at Trump’s rallies.
During tonight’s rally in Georgia, Raphael Warnock, the state’s Democratic senator, described the upcoming election as a “moral moment in America”.
“There are demagogues at the highest levels of our government who are trying to divide us and distract us in order to dominate us, but we come here tonight to say the jig is up.”
Warnock criticized Republicans in Congress for supporting legislation that will take away healthcare from millions of Americans, and cause 1.2 million children to lose access to Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Snap) benefits. He referenced a photo of Republicans praying before voting on Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
“Our nations leaders, led by the speaker of the House, Mike Johnson, gathered together, put their arms around each other and they knelt down to pray, donning the garments of virtue while literally taking food out of the mouths of hungry children,” Warnock said.
Obama campaigns in Georgia as Trump stumps in Ohio in dueling midterm rallies
With midterm elections less than a week away, Donald Trump and Barack Obama were set to appear at rallies on Wednesday night as Republicans and Democrats make some of their final appeals to voters in key states.
Obama, who was recently in Michigan to support Abdul El-Sayed, is in Georgia, where he will campaign for Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor seeking the governor’s office, and the senator Jon Ossoff.
Meanwhile, Donald Trump, who has appeared at more than 20 rallies in October, was returning to the battleground state of Ohio to support Republican candidates, including Vivek Ramaswamy, who is running for governor, and Jon Husted for Senate.
JD Vance was in North Carolina stumping for Michael Whatley, the former RNC chair, who faces a tough race for Senate against Democrat and former governor Roy Cooper.
Donald Trump continued to rail against Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola, accusing her of “Voter Fraud at the Highest Level” following a report from the New York Times that her campaign recruited a man with the same name as her Republican opponent.
In his fourth social media post on the subject in two hours, the president said on Wednesday that Peltola should be removed from the ballot and prosecuted: “Nothing else will do! This behavior in our Elections cannot be allowed to continue.”
Peltola’s campaign recruited the candidate in order to peel away votes, the New York Times reported.
JD Vance echoed Trump’s criticism. “Even the New York Times admits that Mary Peltola is a total crook who tried to rig the Alaska senate race in her favor,” he said.
JD Vance has reportedly contacted Iran’s security chief in an effort to resume peace negotiations.
The Wall Street Journal, citing US officials and others familiar with the matter, reported on Wednesday that the vice-president sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, the hardline leader of Iran’s supreme national security council, at Trump’s urging.
Vance is seeking to determine whether the countries can “find enough common ground” to deter the president from ordering an attack in the near future, according to the outlet.
The development comes just ahead of the midterm elections, and Trump’s deeply unpopular war threatens to hurt Republicans. The US military has already spent over $47bn on the conflict, more than 25% higher than the defense department’s estimate in the summer, according to Pentagon data first obtained by Reuters.
Trump is bound for Ohio to campaign for Republican candidates in the state. Republicans are defending a seat there in a Senate race that has turned out much closer than might’ve been expected in reliably red Ohio. JD Vance, meanwhile, is campaigning in North Carolina, where Republicans face even longer odds.
Obama will campaign in Georgia alongside local Democrats. Obama will join Jon Ossoff, the Democratic senator, and Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor seeking to flip the Georgia governor’s office, on the campaign stage.
Alaska Democrats intentionally recruited a candidate with the same name as their opponent, according to a new report. The New York Times found that Mary Peltola’s campaign had, despite its public denials, recruited a man named Dan Sullivan to run against the Republican incumbent, also named Dan Sullivan. The revelation prompted Trump to call for Peltola’s removal from the ticket.
Flavio Bolsonaro, the defeated rightwing candidate for Brazil’s presidency, landed in Miami. Bolsonaro had been ordered to turn over his passports in connection with a criminal investigation following his defeat by leftwing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Instead, he fled across Brazil’s border with Argentina and flew to the US, where he’s been granted apparent safe harbor by Trump’s state department.
The US Federal Reserve opted to keep interest rates steady. Despite inflation remaining above the central bank’s target of 2%, its leaders chose to maintain interest rates at their current level.
Trump shared another post to social media railing against Mary Peltola and calling for her disqualification over recruiting a second Dan Sullivan into the Senate race:
“In Alaska, I don’t think Mary Peltola, after perpetrating such a terrible scheme, should be allowed to run, because this is ELECTION FRAUD,” Trump wrote. “The Democrats cheated! They found a man named Dan Sullivan, put him on the Ballot, then lied to the Court, and said they didn’t know anything about it. That’s perjury. She shouldn’t be allowed to run, and neither should the FAKE Dan Sullivan!”
Trump rages at Alaska Democrat whose campaign reportedly recruited man with same name as Republican opponent
Donald Trump responded on Wednesday afternoon to a new investigation from the New York Times, which found that Mary Peltola’s Alaska Senate campaign actively recruited a man with the exact same name as Peltola’s Republican opponent in order to peel away votes.
In a social media post, Trump insisted that Peltola’s actions were illegal (it’s not clear that they were) and that she should be disqualified from the race.
“It has just been determined that the Democrats in Alaska illegally searched for, and recruited, a man named Dan Sullivan to run against our distinguished Republican Senator, Dan Sullivan, in order to defraud, confuse, and obfuscate the Election, thereby taking votes away from the REAL Senator, Dan Sullivan,” Trump wrote on his personal social media account.
The Peltola campaign had, up until now, denied any connection to the campaign launched by the second Dan Sullivan, who just so happened to share the name of Dan Sullivan, the Republican incumbent whose Senate seat Peltola is trying to win.
The Department of Justice has moved to try to block the certification of the Alaska Senate race, should the second, non-Republican Mr Sullivan pull enough votes to shift the outcome.
Trump continued: “The Democrats’ false statements were made under oath in Federal Court. Therefore, they perjured themselves, and should be liable for very serious consequences. Mary Peltola should suffer the Legal and Political consequences for what she has done, A FRAUD ON THE AMERICAN PUBLIC, and Dan Sullivan should be allowed to run without either Mary Peltola or FAKE Dan Sullivan on the Ballot.”

article_title: Non-profit group leaks data of more than 40,000 homeland security workers
article_content:
Data identifying more than 41,000 employees and contractors for the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) was released on Wednesday in an unprecedented leak that reveals how the agency is organized. The records, which were made public by the transpaency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets reference operation names, surveillance programs and information on undercover initiatives.
DHS did not immediately return a message seeking comment.
The leaked data unveils the names, phone numbers and email addresses of employees from various DHS agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency.
Most of the agents in the leak – more than 21,000 – work for CBP, and about 6,600 work for ICE.
The data also includes job titles, email groups and other details that show which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance jobs, computer forensics and undercover work.
It was made public at a time when DHS, in turn, has aggressively sought to unmask critics on social media, and obtain records on protestors and journalists – even as it moves to keep its own agents anonymous, defending agents’ rights to hide their identities and faces while conducting enforcement.
In a statement, Emma Best, a Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder, said the hacktivist known as “maia arson crimew” developed a search tool for the data that would allow the public to browse it. Best said the tool would “replace anonymity with accountability” and empower journalists, guide public records requests and boost congressional oversight.
The Department of Peace did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but in a statement included with the data, it said that DHS employees “have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs” and that it hoped the data “can be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction”.
The disclosure – which the non-profit data transparency group says draws on information obtained by an entity calling itself “Department of Peace” – is the third government data leak to have made headlines in the past month.
In September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed the theft of a massive trove of data from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including sensitive job details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees. Last week, the defense department was hit with a class action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel.
The Department of Peace in March claimed responsibility for hacking DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors.
Best’s statement said Department of Peace harvested the data from the Okta sign-on service used by DHS. Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to a Reuters query: “Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised.”
Reuters could not immediately verify the authenticity of the entire data trove but it was able to match personal information of about six DHS employees named in the leak to credit bureau records and breach data carried by the dark web intelligence platform District 4 Labs. In other cases, Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach.
In several cases, the data tracked information available on DHS employees’ LinkedIn profiles. But in others, the data revealed nonpublic data about internal DHS organization charts or previously undisclosed programs or operations.

article_title: "Розверніться, поки ще є час": сенатор США вимагає зупинити постачання російського дизеля
article_content:
"Розверніться, поки ще є час": сенатор США вимагає зупинити постачання російського дизеля
У США заявили про незаконність імпорту російського дизеля. Сенатор вимагає розвернути танкери.
Сенатор США Річард Блюменталь закликав судноплавні компанії розвернути танкери з російським дизелем. Він наголосив, що ввезення цього пального до Америки є незаконним.
Про це сенатор від Демократичної партії повідомив у соцмережі Х.
Законодавець звернувся до морських перевізників, чий флот задіяний у доставці російського пального до американських портів.
«Змініть курс, поки ще є час», — наголосив він.
Зокрема, сенатор надіслав листа керівникові грецької компанії EASTMED Атанасіосу Мартіносу щодо танкера Agioi Fanendes. Судно під прапором Мальти вийшло з російського порту 22 жовтня майже з 40 тисячами тонн дизеля і має прибути до порту Нью-Йорка та Нью-Джерсі 7 листопада.
Сенатор вимагає від компанії до 31 жовтня надати дані про всіх учасників угоди: продавця, покупця, фрахтувальника, страховика, оператора термінала та дистриб’ютора. Крім того, він просить уточнити, чи отримувала компанія якісь вказівки від Мінфіну США.
Блюменталь підкреслив, що розвантаження цього пального порушує закон 2022 року Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act. За його словами, генеральна ліцензія № 135 від Мінфіну США не може скасувати заборону, встановлену законодавчим органом.
«Президент, можливо, видав ліцензію для сприяння цій операції, але лише Конгрес може зробити її юридично чинною», — заявив Блюменталь.
Політик підсумував, що жодні ліцензії не звільнять компанії від відповідальності за порушення закону.
«Розверніться, поки ще є час. Якщо ви доставите дизель, ви порушите цілком однозначний закон, ухвалений у 2022 році, який забороняє імпорт російського пального. Жоден президент не може одноосібно скасувати закон», — зазначив сенатор.
Дизельна угода Трампа та Путіна — останні новини
Нагадаємо, три танкери з приблизно 140 тисячами тонн російського дизелю прямують до США в межах домовленості Дональда Трампа з Володимиром Путіним. Серед них — судно Leruo, яке перебуває під санкціями ЄС, Великої Британії та Канади.
Раніше ТСН.ua писав, що дизельна угода між Дональдом Трампом і Володимиром Путіним викликала критику як в Україні, так і у США. У Вашингтоні група сенаторів від обох партій поставила під сумнів законність домовленості, посилаючись на ухвалену 2022 року заборону на імпорт російської нафти.

article_title: У Путіна сказали, від чого буде залежати продовження переговорів про мир
article_content:
У Путіна сказали, від чого буде залежати продовження переговорів про мир
Росія очікує підсумків проміжних виборів у США 3 листопада, перш ніж повертатися до тристоронніх переговорів про завершення війни в Україні.
Росія готова відновити тристоронні переговори щодо закінчення війни в Україні після 4 листопада.
Про це заявив помічник диктатора Путіна Юрій Ушаков, якого цитують російські пропагандистські ЗМІ.
Очевидно, ця дата пов’язана з тим, що в США на 3 листопада заплановані проміжні вибори до Конгресу.
Ушаков ухильно відповів, що терміни продовження переговорів залежатимуть «від розвитку ситуації, включаючи становище на фронті».
«Це ясно, що буде після 4 листопада», — сказав він пропагандистам.
Судячи із заяви Ушакова, в Кремлі ще остаточно не визначилися зі складом переговорної групи. За його словами, склад делегації Росії визначать найближчим часом. Ушаков при цьому зазначив, що «кістяк делегації є».
Також він повідомив, що кандидатури Стубба і Стере як представники всієї Європи на переговорах поки не обговорюються.
Раніше Ушаков заявив, що європейські країни не братимуть участі у переговорах між Росією, Україною та США.
Нагадаємо, в інтерв’ю британським ЗМІ президент Володимир Зеленський повідомив, переговори між Україною, США та Росією щодо завершення війни можуть відбутися вже 10 листопада в Абу-Дабі — одразу після проміжних виборів у Сполучених Штатах.
Проте на сьогоднішньому брифінгу з прем’єром Нідерландів Зеленський уточнив, що точна дата переговорів із Володимиром Путіним поки невідома, адже це повністю залежить від рішення Кремля.

article_title: Рік УПА на Львівщині, який обурив Польщу, під питанням: Козицький зробив заяву
article_content:
Рік УПА на Львівщині, який обурив Польщу, під питанням: Козицький зробив заяву
У Польщі занепокоїлися рішенням Львівської облради оголосити 2027 рік роком УПА. Голова Львівської ОВА Максим Козицький повідомив, на якому етапі зараз це рішення та чи набуло воно чинності.
Рішення Львівської обласної ради оголосити 2027 рік роком УПА поки не підписане й не набрало чинності. Про це у відповідь на занепокоєння Польщі заявив голова Львівської ОВА Максим Козицький.
Про це повідомляє Польське агентство преси (PAP).
«Хочу повідомити Вас, що рішення Львівської обласної ради, про яке йдеться у Вашому листі, ще не підписано та не набуло чинності. Переконаний, що рішення органів влади всіх рівнів повинні враховувати інтереси зовнішньої політики України та добросусідські відносини з Республікою Польща», — зазначив Максим Козицький.
Голова ОДА наголосив, що усвідомлює чутливість питань історичної пам’яті для обох народів, та закликав до обговорення таких тем в атмосфері взаємної поваги й відкритості. Він також подякував партнерам за підтримку України та допомогу біженцям під час російської агресії.
Скандал через рік УПА у Львові — останні новини
Нагадаємо, рішення про оголошення 2027 року роком УПА, її командира Романа Шухевича та діяча ОУН Олега Ольжича Львівська обласна рада ухвалила на засіданні 20 жовтня.
Навіть Міністерство закордонних справ України назвало це рішення «контрпродуктивним», підкресливши, що воно було ухвалене на регіональному рівні без жодних консультацій із дипломатами.
Ініціатором відповідної постанови був депутат облради Святослав Шеремета. Після цього міністр закордонних справ Польщі Радослав Сікорський заявив, що звернувся до Управління у справах іноземців із проханням внести його до списку небажаних осіб у Польщі.
Згодом польське Люблінське воєводство припинило співпрацю зі Львівською областю через це рішення облради.
